name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since 5 Feb
summary: No US–Russia arms limits since New START lapsed; an IAEA report says Iran links stalled monitoring to US threats
state: New START expired on 5 Feb and the US rejected Russia's offer to keep its central limits; Arms Control Today's November issue reports US threats to respond in kind to any low-yield testing by others and a US vote against a UN test-moratorium resolution in October. A confidential IAEA report on 13 Nov said Iran told the agency that monitoring talks cannot proceed under military threat (AP via Just Security). No nuclear test, change in alert levels or explicit threat of use was found as of 13 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: No public safety action is needed. National emergency agencies publish general preparedness guidance. Arms-control lapses tend to raise the risk of miscalculation over time rather than signal an immediate threat.
rubric_hit: Watch: arms-control lapse without replacement (New START expired 5 Feb); no test, alert change or threatened use

sources.title: Arms Control Association — Nuclear-Weapon States Consult as Trump Talks Denuclearization

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
